research_rationale: EO 10195 (Dec. 20, 1950; 15 FR 9177) designated Korea and the adjacent waters within stated limits as a combat zone under section 22(b)(13) of the Internal Revenue Code (as amended by the Revenue Act of 1950) and fixed June 27, 1950 as the date combatant activities commenced there. EO 10585 (signed Jan. 1, 1955; 20 FR 17) was issued under section 112(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 and designates January 31, 1955, as of midnight thereof, as the date of termination of combatant activities in the zone comprised of the area described in EO 10195. The OFR note points to EO 10585 with the signing date Jan. 1, 1955, but that is the date of the instrument; the termination date it designates is January 31, 1955. A combat-zone designation exists only for the period between the commencement date and the termination date, so the designation ended at midnight closing 1955-01-31 (inclusive reading; the exclusive reading is that it ended when Feb. 1, 1955 began). EO 10195 has no own-terms end and no other held instrument revokes or amends it; EO 10585 is the only later instrument naming it. Residual: tax consequences for service within June 27, 1950 to Jan. 31, 1955 accrued and are a surviving effect of the designation rather than a continuing command.
savings_reason: The designation operated for the period June 27, 1950 through the termination date. The tax-exclusion consequences that attached to service in the zone during that period (and the 1952 public law text held in the corpus that defines Korea by reference to EO 10195) are accrued effects of a completed designation. EO 10585 does not cancel them and no held source shows a continuing command in EO 10195.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for citations of Executive Order 10195 by number: six held files cite it (EO 10585, the Federal Register page, a 1952 Public Law citing the zone and the 1989 OFR codification text). Only EO 10585 acts on the zone. The order has no own-terms expiry; the until and effective signals in the text come from neighbouring documents on the same Federal Register page. The current-law searches (U.S. Code and eCFR) had no hit naming EO 10195.
scope_check: The order is one paragraph with two designations: the area (Korea and adjacent waters) and the commencement date. EO 10585 terminates combatant activities in the zone comprised of the area described in EO 10195, so the area designation is spent as of the termination date; the commencement date is the start of the period and has no independent forward command. The clause inventory keeps the single whole-order clause.
independent_command_check: No clause is independent: the commencement date only fixes the start of the period over which the designation runs, and ends with it. A later statutory or tax rule that refers to the zone by period is a separate effect (see savings), not a command of EO 10195.

research_rationale: EO 11202 (Mar. 5, 1965; 30 FR 3185) directed that a Schedule B Student Trainee in a shortage occupation be converted to a career or career-conditional appointment if four conditions were met (Sec. 1 items (1)-(4)), defined a cooperative work-study program (Sec. 2) and told the Civil Service Commission to prescribe regulations (Sec. 3). Section 4 of EO 11813 (signed Oct. 7, 1974; 39 FR 36317) states "Executive Order No. 11202 of March 5, 1965, is hereby revoked." and Section 5 states "This order shall become effective immediately." The order is a standing conversion rule with no term of its own, so the express revocation is its first and only end: all four dossier clauses end together on 1974-10-07. The cross-check is the held 5 U.S.C. 3301 note in jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s3301.txt, which states that Executive Order No. 11202 "was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 11813, Oct. 7, 1974, 39 F.R. 36317". No earlier end was found: the only later-event records are EO 11813 (revocation) and the U.S. Code note citing it.
savings_reason: Conversions to career or career-conditional appointments completed under Section 1 before Oct. 7, 1974 were executed acts. EO 11813 Section 4 revokes EO 11202 without any language undoing them, and no held source shows a continuing independent command. Appointments already made survive as accrued status; the conversion authority itself ended on 1974-10-07.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for citations of Executive Order 11202 by number: the only later instrument that revokes, supersedes or amends it is EO 11813 (Oct. 7, 1974). The order's own text has no expiry date, sunset or until-condition (own-text signals empty), so nothing ends it earlier than EO 11813 Section 4. The OFR catalog notes Revoked by EO 11813, October 7, 1974 and Revokes EO 11202, March 5, 1965, and the dossier chain records no other event.
scope_check: The revocation in EO 11813 Section 4 names EO 11202 in full and is not limited to a part, so every clause (Sec. 1 items (1)-(4), Sec. 2 definition and Sec. 3 regulation direction) ends on the same day. The dossier's fourth clause span runs from item (4) to the end of the order and so also covers Sections 2 and 3.
independent_command_check: Section 1 (conversion command), Section 2 (definition used only by Section 1) and Section 3 (Commission to prescribe regulations to carry out the provisions of the order) are not independent of one another; the Commission regulations depend on the order and the held sources show no separate statute or order preserving them. Revocation by EO 11813 ends all of them together.
savings_check: See savings_reason: accrued conversions survive; no independent continuing command was found in the held sources.

research_rationale: EO 11813 (Oct. 7, 1974; 39 FR 36317) directed that a cooperative education student under a Schedule B appointment may be converted noncompetitively to a career or career-conditional appointment if four conditions in Section 2 items (1)-(4) are met, defined cooperative education (Sec. 1), directed the Civil Service Commission to issue regulations (Sec. 3), revoked EO 11202 (Sec. 4) and took effect immediately (Sec. 5). Section 4 of EO 12015 (signed Oct. 26, 1977; 42 FR 56947) states, in the Federal Register OCR text, "Executive Order No. 11813 of October 7, 1974-, is hereby revoked." The American Presidency Project page for EO 12015 gives the same sentence cleanly: "Executive Order No. 11813 of October 7, 1974, is hereby revoked." EO 12015 contains no effective-date clause, so the revocation operates from its signing date. The cross-check is the held 5 U.S.C. 3301 note in jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s3301.txt, which states that Executive Order No. 11813 "was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12015, Oct. 26, 1977, 42 F.R. 56947". The order has no own-terms end, so the express revocation is its first end and all four dossier clauses end together on 1977-10-26.
savings_reason: Conversions completed under Section 2 before Oct. 26, 1977 were executed acts and EO 12015 Section 4 does not undo them. EO 12015 sets a similar conversion rule for career-related work-study programs, but that is a new command in a new order, not a continuation of EO 11813. No held source shows an independent command that still depends on EO 11813.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for citations of Executive Order 11813 by number: the only instrument that revokes, supersedes or amends it is EO 12015 (Oct. 26, 1977). The OFR catalog notes Revoked by EO 12015, October 26, 1977. The order has no expiry, sunset or until-condition, and the dossier chain shows no earlier event.
scope_check: EO 12015 Section 4 revokes Executive Order No. 11813 of October 7, 1974 in full, not in part, so all clauses end together. Section 4 of EO 11813 itself revoked EO 11202; that revocation was executed on Oct. 7, 1974 and is a performed act which the later revocation of EO 11813 does not revive.
independent_command_check: Sections 1 (definition), 2 (conversion rule), 3 (Commission regulations) and 5 (effective date) all depend on the single conversion rule; none is an independent command that would outlive it. The Sec. 4 revocation of EO 11202 was completed on its effective date and is not an operative command at the 2026 cutoff.

research_rationale: EO 12576 (Dec. 2, 1986) delegated to the Secretary of State the President's functions under section 803 of the Act (5 U.S.C. 5569) and to the Secretary of Defense those under section 806 (37 U.S.C. 559), each for paying compensation to individuals held in captive status commencing on or before January 21, 1981, and directed the two Secretaries to consult (Secs. 1-3). EO 12598 (signed June 17, 1987; 52 FR 23421, Monday, June 22, 1987), issued to implement the same Title VIII of Public Law 99-399, restates the delegations of section 803(a) functions (5 U.S.C. 5569) to the Secretary of State (Sec. 1) and of section 806(a) functions (37 U.S.C. 559) to the Secretary of Defense (Sec. 3), repeats the consultation duty (Sec. 5) and states "Executive Order No. 12576 of December 2,1986, is hereby superseded." (Sec. 6). The delegations are therefore replaced, not merely ended: express supersession is the first end of all three clauses on 1987-06-17 (EO 12598 has no separate effective-date clause, so it operates from its signing date; the Federal Register publication date, June 22, 1987, is not the effective date). The order has no term of its own and no earlier end was found in the held sources; the OFR catalog records Superseded by EO 12598, June 17, 1987.
savings_reason: The functions were delegated, not performed once: EO 12598 Secs. 1, 3 and 5 re-delegate the same section 803 and 806 functions to the same Secretaries and repeat the consultation duty, so the delegated authority was transferred rather than extinguished. scope_check: EO 12598 Section 6 supersedes Executive Order No. 12576 of December 2,1986 in full, with no limitation to part, so all three sections end together. An abolished-office or liquidation question does not arise: the order delegates presidential functions, and EO 12598 re-delegates them.
independent_command_check: Section 3 (consultation between the Secretaries) serves the delegations in Sections 1 and 2 and is repeated in EO 12598 Section 5; Sections 1 and 2 are each repeated in EO 12598 Sections 1 and 3. None is an independent command left standing after the supersession.
